readout_other: 60-channel microelectrode array spontaneous spike counts by threshold level and subregion
direction_notes: Normalized spontaneous spike counts, mainly large spikes, increased after (and for level 3 also during) ultrasound relative to sham; abolished by kynurenic acid or TTX.

exposures.label: Unfocused pulsed ultrasound over organotypic hippocampal slice, 0.5 MHz, 3 min

device.model: water-immersion transducer (10 x 10 mm square crystal element)

timing.protocol_description: 3 min of baseline recording, 3 min of unfocused pulsed ultrasound (or sham, pulser off), then 3 min of recording; pulse duration 2.097 microseconds at 1.16 kHz PRF.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Using a 60-channel multielectrode array (MEA), we measured spontaneous spiking across organotypic rat hippocampal slice cultures (N 5 28) for 3 min each before, during, and after stimulation with low-intensity unfocused pulsed or sham ultrasound (spatial-peak pulse average intensity 780 lW/cm<sup>2</sup>) preperfused with artificial cerebrospinal fluid, 300 lM kynurenic acid (KA), or 0.5 lM tetrodotoxin (TTX) at 3 ml/ min.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In this study, we used a 60-channel multielectrode array (MEA) to measure spontaneous population spike activity in dentate gyrus (DG), CA3, CA2, and CA1 in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures from 7-day-old Sprague-Dawley rats before, during, and after 3 min of stimulation with centered unfocused pulsed ultrasound (center frequency 0.5 MHz, pulse duration 2.097 lsec, pulse repetition frequency 1.16 kHz) or sham.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: Spatial peak pressure amplitude was measured to be 11.52 kPa; spatial-peak pulse-average intensity (I<sub>SPPA</sub>) was calculated from pressure signals per industry standards (NEMA, 2004).
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.isppa_w_cm2: The x and y dimensions of focus of the half-pressure maximum was approximately 8.5 3 8.5 mm, within which the I<sub>SPPA</sub> came to 780 lW/cm<sup>2</sup> (Fig. 1).
